title: Climbing Kilimanjaro With Teenagers
excerpt: The minimum age to climb to the summit of Kilimanjaro is 10. Here is how to prepare teenagers, which route to choose and what to keep an eye on.
body:
Climbing Kilimanjaro with your teenager can be a shared adventure you both remember for life. The national park allows children from the age of 10 to attempt the summit. Younger children can do day walks or lower treks.

## Is your teenager ready?

Ask honestly: does your child enjoy long walks? Can they cope with cold, simple toilets and early mornings? Do they want to go, or is it mainly your dream? Motivation matters on summit night.

## Route and days

Choose a route with good acclimatisation and a gentle profile, such as [Lemosho in eight days](/blog/kilimanjaro-lemosho-route-guide/) or [Rongai in seven](/blog/kilimanjaro-rongai-route-guide/). Avoid short programmes.

## Health checks

Young people can get altitude symptoms just like adults, and they sometimes hide them. Agree beforehand that they tell the guide honestly how they feel. Guides check oxygen levels twice a day.

## Train together

Long weekend walks together are good training and good for motivation. Our [12-week training plan](/blog/kilimanjaro-training-plan/) works for teenagers too.

## Keep it fun

- Bring cards or a small game for camp.
- Let them help plan: route, kit, snacks.
- Celebrate small goals: the Barranco Wall, the first glacier view.

## Afterwards

Teenagers usually love a [safari](/blog/kilimanjaro-and-safari-combined/) or a few days on the beach after the climb. See our [family travel](/family-tours/) ideas and [plan your trip](/travel-proposal/).
